user.title: Lightweight Status Badge
user.description: Set up the integration, then use Configure to manage rules. This is a Devices & services integration, not a helper.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge alert
acknowledge.description: Set or revoke the global acknowledgement for the current occurrence.

init.title: Rule management
init.description:
**{count} rules** (preview: up to 10). ✓ enabled, ⏸ disabled. Find all rules under Select existing rule.

{rules}

edit.title: Edit rule
edit.description: Draft: **{rule}** · {entity}. Accept pages with Apply / continue. Only Save rule activates the changes. Entities remaining after this one: {remaining}.

remove.title: Remove rule
remove.description: Removes the rule and its current acknowledgement. The source entity remains available.

source.title: Source entity
source.description: Select an existing entity or enter an entity ID. Only use on as a fault for an explicitly selected fault indicator.

preset.title: Apply template
preset.description: Entity: **{entity}**. Entities remaining after this one: {remaining}. Templates replace the draft trigger, severity, explanation and availability defaults. Review before saving.

trigger.title: Trigger condition
trigger.description: Type: {kind}. Add set members separately. Custom rules use the text/number or set according to the operator. UPS: OB = on battery, LB = low battery, FSD = forced shutdown, RB = replace battery; LB/FSD are critical. Other tokens do not trigger a fault. Entity: **{entity}**. For fault states, check values that should trigger an alert; other values do not trigger this rule. For drive health, healthy states are instead the allowed values. Suggestions come from declared options, standard HA activities and the current state. Lists may be incomplete; add custom values as needed. unknown/unavailable use the separate availability policies.

details.title: Title, messages and availability
details.description: An empty explanation uses the translated, state-specific template message (including UPS). Placeholders: `{state_placeholder}` and `{attribute_placeholder}`; NAME must be in the attribute list. No Python or Jinja. Changes apply only after Save rule.

pick_source.title: Add entities
pick_source.description: Choose a device or integration instance, then check the entities you want to monitor. You can also select an entity directly.

device.title: Choose device
device.description: The next step lists all entities belonging to this device.

integration.title: Choose integration
integration.description: If an integration has multiple instances, choose the relevant entry.

entities.title: Check entities
entities.description: All associated entities are shown, including vacuum/mower operating entities and hidden or disabled entities. Disabled entities provide states only after you enable them in Home Assistant; this flow does not enable them. Configure and save a separate rule for each selected entity. Cancelling discards only unsaved rules.

error.invalid_trigger: Check the trigger: use a finite number, suitable entity and nonempty state lists.
error.invalid_rule: Invalid rule. Check fields, text lengths (max 1000), attribute names (max 10), unique IDs and rule count (max 1000).
error.rule_changed: The rule changed while editing. Discard this draft and reopen the rule.
error.invalid_device: The device is no longer available.
error.invalid_integration: The integration instance is no longer available.
error.no_entities: No registered entities found. Choose another source or enter the entity directly.
error.source_changed: The source changed. Select the entities again.
error.too_many_rules: This selection would exceed the limit of 1000 rules.
